official.deadline_note: There are no submission deadlines for this program; applications can be submitted at any time via elane. The FWF review process usually takes about 4 to 6 months and the Scientific Board holds five approval meetings per year.
official.application_cycle: Rolling submissions year-round; decisions taken at five FWF Scientific Board approval meetings per year
official.status_note: ESPRIT is listed in the FWF funding portfolio with rolling submissions; the FWF states that applications can be submitted at any time and that there are no submission deadlines for this program.
official.tuition_coverage_note: ESPRIT funds the principal investigator's full-time employment at the host institution, not a degree programme or study fees. The published funding description covers the principal investigator's salary and project-specific costs only; no statement about tuition fees is made. The FWF also states that it does not finance the infrastructure or basic equipment of research institutions.
official.funding_period: per year (gross, incl. employer contributions), 2026 rate
benefits: Full-time employment of the principal investigator for the 36-month project duration, with the salary funded through the project at the current senior postdoc rate
Lump sum of EUR 45,000 for project-specific costs, of which up to EUR 6,000 can be used for coaching and/or professional development
A total of up to EUR 75,000 in project-specific costs upon justified request, with a full cost breakdown in the project description

Child allowance of EUR 9,600 per child per year (gross salary including all employer and employee taxes, paid out 12 times a year) for female principal investigators employed full time, up until the child's third birthday
A mentor to support the principal investigator's scientific and professional development, employed at least 20% at an Austrian research institution
Networking activities, annual workshops and measures to increase visibility for women involved in ESPRIT projects
eligibility: The program is addressed to highly qualified postdocs of all disciplines from Austria and abroad at the beginning of their academic career
The doctoral degree of principal investigators must have been awarded no more than five years at the time of application, calculated from the date of the successful thesis defence exam

At least two quality-assured and internationally visible publications from the last five calendar years with a substantial and independent contribution by the applicant, and at least one publication with first, last, or corresponding authorship
A mentor working in Austria, employed at least 20% at an Austrian research institution, to support the career development of the principal investigator
The project must be carried out in Austria under the auspices of the applying Austrian research institution, which must provide the necessary infrastructure

Persons who already hold a position at the applying research institution with the prospect of permanent employment (e.g., tenure track) or a permanent research contract cannot serve as principal investigator unless the contract is linked to third-party funding, researchers who have completed a habilitation are also excluded, and in the ESPRIT program researchers can serve only once as principal investigator
requirements: Applications must be submitted in English to allow review by international peers; submission solely in German or another specialist language is permitted only in exceptional cases in linguistic and literary studies involving texts other than English, after prior consultation with the FWF Career Programs department
A career and mentoring plan of no more than 3 pages, written together with the mentor, is mandatory

A 100% employment contract for the principal investigator must be requested for the entire duration of the project; any existing fixed-term employment must be withdrawn from or a leave of absence taken for the project duration
It is not possible to submit parallel applications in the other FWF career programs Erwin Schroedinger or FWF ASTRA Awards
Metrics such as journal impact factors, Article Influence Scores, or the h-index may not be included in the application

All proposals must be submitted online using the elane digital application portal; project funding is administered through the research institutions (PROFI) and the application must be approved for submission by both the applicant and the lead research institution, and at least two reviews are required for approval of an application
documents: Proposal.pdf: project description of no more than 20 consecutively numbered pages including the table of contents, plus Annex 1 (references, max. 5 pages), Annex 2 (CVs of the principal investigator and the mentor, max. 3 pages each), Annex 3 (career and mentoring plan, max. 3 pages) and optional Annex 4 (collaboration letters, max. 1 page each), with PDF bookmarks for the major sections

PI_publication.pdf: two publications from the last five calendar years documenting that the applicant fulfils the publication record requirements, using the FWF template publication record of the principal investigator

Publication_lists.pdf: publication lists of the principal investigator and the mentor for the last five calendar years, categorized as quality-assured publications and other publications, in one single document

Online forms: Research institution assignment, Contact form, Application form, Program-specific data, Cost breakdown, Academic abstract (in English) and Co-authors; Associated research partner and Other cooperation where applicable

Where applicable: Cover_Letter.pdf, Negative_list.pdf (up to 3 reviewers to be excluded, with justification), Follow.pdf for follow-up applications, Overview_revision.pdf and Revision.pdf for resubmissions
For approved projects: PR summaries in German and English, a data management plan using the FWF template, and the mentor's signed declaration of support, submitted together with the funding agreement
selection_criteria: Innovation or novelty, and quality of the proposed research
Research-related qualifications of the principal investigator
Contribution of the research project to the career development of the principal investigator, the suitability of the mentor, and the planned career development measures
Suitability of the research institution for implementing the planned project and the project's contribution to enhancing the research institution, plus the reviewers' overall evaluation
coverage: Principal investigator's salary at the current senior postdoc rate for a 36-month full-time employment; the FWF's standard senior postdoc personnel cost rate valid from January 2026 is EUR 97,380.00 per year / EUR 5,499.10 per month at 40 hours per week, including the employer's contribution (gross salary)

Project-specific costs from EUR 45,000 as a flat-rate lump sum to up to EUR 75,000 upon request with justification and a full cost breakdown; eligible categories are personnel costs, equipment costs, material costs, travel costs (including presentation of project results at conferences), contracts for work and services, and other eligible costs
Up to EUR 6,000 of the project-specific funds may be used for coaching and/or professional development
Child allowance of EUR 9,600 per child per year for female principal investigators employed full time after the birth of a child, up until the child's third birthday
application_method: Online application through the elane digital application portal, administered in PROFI mode: after logging in, select "Application PROFI" (not "Application ad personam") and then the funding category "ESP - ESPRIT Program"

All forms must be completed online; the project description including annexes and any additional documents must be uploaded in full before the application can be approved for submission by the lead research institution
Applications are submitted by the Austrian research institution where the project is to be carried out; research institutions must be registered in the FWF's research institution portal
official.application_route: Rolling online submission via the elane portal in PROFI mode, submitted through a registered Austrian research institution whose approval is required before the application reaches the FWF.
official.study_mode: Full-time (a 100% employment contract for the principal investigator must be requested for the entire duration of the project)
official.citizenship_residency: Open to researchers from Austria and abroad; the FWF states that the territoriality principle does not apply to the ESPRIT program, so no Austrian citizenship or prior research in Austria is required. All Austrian research institutions are eligible to apply, and the project must be carried out in Austria.
official.international_eligibility: Yes. The program is addressed to highly qualified postdocs of all disciplines from Austria and abroad, and because the territoriality principle does not apply to ESPRIT, applications can be submitted from abroad. An Austrian mentor and an Austrian host research institution are still required.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: All disciplines are eligible, including arts-based research. Clinical research projects may also be funded if they are clearly defined in objectives and methods, limited in time and budget, and their results are not connected with direct commercial interests; a positive opinion from the relevant ethics commission or evidence of a fundamental approval/endorsement must be attached.
official.research_requirement: A clearly defined, innovative basic research project limited in duration, with plausibly described objectives and methods and specific hypotheses or research questions. Incremental further development of published data is not considered innovative or original. The project must contribute to the principal investigator developing an independent research profile.
official.description: The ESPRIT (Early-Stage Program: Research, Innovation, Training) aims to foster the career development of researchers from all disciplines at the beginning of their academic career who wish to carry out an independent research project at an Austrian research institution, with the principal investigator supported in their skills and career development by a mentor. The FWF's stated objectives are to fund excellent, innovative research; to retain, attract, and win back outstanding researchers and thus strengthen Austrian research institutions; to support outstanding women researchers; and to build independent research profiles. The FWF places particular emphasis on the promotion of women and aims to award at least half of the projects in the program to female principal investigators.
official.region: Austria (project must be carried out in Austria); catalogue region: Europe
official.program_type: Career development program for early-career postdocs (principal investigator project), administered in PROFI mode by the Austrian Science Fund (FWF)
official.english_requirement: Applications must be submitted in English to allow them to be reviewed by international peers, and the academic abstract must be written in English (max. 3,000 characters including spaces). A German or other-language version may be added as a supplement; submission solely in German or another specialist language is only permitted in exceptional cases for applications from linguistic and literary studies involving texts other than English, and requires prior consultation with the FWF Career Programs department. No English language test is required.

not_confirmed: funding_amount as a single total award: the FWF publishes the principal investigator's salary as the standard senior postdoc personnel cost rate plus a project lump sum, not a combined total grant amount
tuition_coverage: ESPRIT funds an employment position, and no statement about tuition or study fees is published
deadline_central: the FWF states there are no submission deadlines for this program, so no deadline date exists to record
verification.notes: Funding figures, eligibility, application route and FAQ verified on the FWF ESPRIT programme page and the Application Guidelines ESPRIT (effective 24 February 2026, version 1.0); the senior postdoc salary rate was taken from the FWF Personnel Costs and Salary Rates page, valid from January 2026, which explicitly names ESPRIT under the senior postdoc category.

applicant_utility.summary: Treat ESPRIT as a three-year salaried research position rather than a travel scholarship: you are employed at 100% at an Austrian research institution, FWF pays your senior postdoc salary and adds a EUR 45,000 project lump sum you can partly spend on coaching. Because you cannot apply directly, the sequencing that matters most is securing an Austrian host institution and a mentor first, since the mentor must hold at least a 20% position in Austria and should not have supervised your own doctorate. Submissions are open all year, but each round still runs roughly 4 to 6 months before the Scientific Board decides, so plan backwards from the date you actually need funding to start.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Postdocs within five years of their thesis defence who already have internationally visible, quality-assured publications and can bring both an Austrian host institution and a credible mentor on board.
application_readiness_checklist: Check the exact date of your successful thesis defence against the five-year rule before writing anything, because eligibility is counted from that date, not from graduation or conferment

Read the FWF project number limit document first, since the number of ongoing and approved projects per principal investigator is capped and a pending Erwin Schroedinger or ASTRA application blocks an ESPRIT submission
Approach the host institution early and confirm it is registered in the FWF research institution portal and willing to approve the submission in PROFI mode

Agree the mentor in advance: at least a 20% position at an Austrian research institution, no previous supervision of your master's, diploma, or dissertation, and time to co-write the career and mentoring plan

Draft Proposal.pdf to the strict page limits, 20 pages for the project description including the table of contents, 5 pages for references, 3 pages each for the PI and mentor CVs and 3 pages for the career and mentoring plan, with PDF bookmarks for the major sections, then build PI_publication.pdf on the FWF template and Publication_lists.pdf covering the last five calendar years split into quality-assured and other publications

Cost the budget honestly: on the standard flat route you request only the senior postdoc personnel line plus a EUR 15,000 'Other costs' lump sum per year, and you add a full cost breakdown only if you need up to EUR 75,000
common_rejection_risks: The publication record fails the formal test: at least two quality-assured, internationally visible publications with substantial independent contribution, one of them with first, last, or corresponding authorship unless the field ranks authors alphabetically
The project description never states specific hypotheses or research questions, which is one of the three most common reasons applications are returned without review
A resubmission is not genuinely revised: applications rejected on C3, C4, or C5 grounds and returned without substantial change based on the previous reviews
The proposal reads as the next logical step or a further development of published data, which the guidelines explicitly exclude from what counts as innovative basic research
Mentoring is treated as paper work: the mentor's suitability and the career and mentoring plan are one of the eight review criteria and must be co-written and internally consistent

Mandatory content is skipped: the guidelines require a brief statement on ethical, safety, regulatory, and sex- and gender-related aspects even when you believe they do not apply, while the 20-page limit also counts tables, figures, and abbreviation lists and impact factors, article influence scores, or h-index values are banned outright
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Your own position is salaried for the full 36 months, so the gaps are the ordinary ones: income tax and social security deductions from gross salary, any shortfall between the FWF standard senior postdoc rate and your host institution's actual collective bargaining rate, relocation and living costs incurred before the project start, and anything the host counts as its own infrastructure. The FWF explicitly does not finance research institutions' basic infrastructure or equipment, and publication costs cannot be requested through this programme.
document_audit: CVs must use the prescribed structure: no photos, ORCID or other researcher identifier, education milestones with dates, positions with the extent of employment, listed career breaks, and only ten most important publications and ten additional research achievements
The PI CV must state net research experience in years and months, split into time before and after the doctorate, since that is how reviewers judge academic age
The academic abstract must stay within 3,000 characters including spaces, use the five prescribed English headings, and name the mentor among the primary researchers
Impact factors, article influence scores, and h-index values must be stripped out of every document under the FWF's compliance with the Agreement on Reforming Research Assessment
Any use of AI tools in preparing the proposal must be described in the Co-authors form, and the FWF checks applications and reviews for plagiarism and AI use randomly and on suspicion

You may submit up to three reviewers you want excluded with a justification, but the FWF will not accept a suggested-reviewer list, and additional unsolicited documents such as recommendation letters are ignored
alerts: There is no deadline, so the real constraint is the 4 to 6 month review plus the two approvals needed inside the institution before submission; time your application for when the funding actually has to begin
You can serve only once as an ESPRIT principal investigator, and you cannot hold a parallel application in the Erwin Schroedinger or FWF ASTRA Awards career programs

A tenure-track or otherwise permanent research contract at the applying institution disqualifies you as PI unless it is linked to third-party funding, and a completed habilitation excludes you outright
A C5 rejection bars the research topic for 12 months, and three rejections on C3 or C4 grounds across the original application and two resubmissions also trigger a 12-month ban

Once the review process has started, no further changes are possible; the only window for corrections is the FWF Office's rectification request, generally allowing 3 weeks, submitted before the deadline as a supplementary application

If the project is approved, the data management plan and the mentor's signed declaration of support must go back with the funding agreement, and the project title, grant amount, and PR summaries in German and English are published
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: You assemble Proposal.pdf, PI_publication.pdf and Publication_lists.pdf plus the online forms in elane under Application PROFI and ESP - ESPRIT Program, the lead research institution approves the submission, and the FWF Office checks for completeness and formal errors before starting international review.
